request.raw: Use FinRunbook to compare how Zoom, DocuSign, Shopify, Etsy and Peloton converted pandemic-era growth into subsequent operating performance from 2019 through 2025. Establish clearly dated pre-pandemic baselines and compare indexed revenue, gross margins, operating profitability, free cash flow, headcount and stock-based compensation where disclosed. Separate expansion, adjustment and subsequent performance, without assuming that every company followed the same trajectory. Account for acquisitions, divestitures, restructuring charges and fiscal-calendar differences. Assess which companies retained a larger business with stronger cash generation, and which conclusions remain uncertain. Produce an English interactive report with indexed historical charts, phase comparisons and a profitability-and-cash-conversion matrix. Cite material inputs and complete final validation.

evidence.content: Management attributes improved operating cash flow to lower operating expenses following restructuring and improved gross profit. Lower hardware demand and fewer paid subscriptions weighed on revenue. This is management attribution, not a causal experiment.

evidence.content: The FY2022 report reclassifies immaterial FY2020–FY2021 income-statement amounts. Those later figures are used. Its cash-flow statement reports capex $0.1 million above the MD&A reconciliation in FY2020 and FY2021; the statement controls here. FY2019 is from the earlier filing.

Shopify lets employees allocate compensation between cash and equity, within restrictions. This can change reported cash and stock-based expenses without identifying a corresponding productivity change.
Workvivo was acquired on April 21, 2023, during Zoom FY2024. Zoom says the included operating results were not material; no organic revenue adjustment is made here.
Lexion was acquired on May 31, 2024, during FY2025. The accounts include associated compensation and acquisition costs. Reported consolidated growth is not labeled organic growth.
Precor was acquired on April 1, 2021, within Peloton FY2021. Later consolidated financial and workforce totals therefore cover a broader business than the FY2019 baseline.
Reverb was acquired in 2019; Depop and Elo7 were acquired in July 2021. The acquired marketplaces enter reported financial metrics from their acquisition dates.
